audit.whatIsWrong: Seven fields describe Feast as 'a true-damage percent execute' that 'ignores your shield' and can 'execute you out of a 50%-HP screen'. Riot's text says Feast devours a unit for a high amount of TRUE DAMAGE, and if the target is killed Cho'Gath grows. There is no percentage of health in the description, no execute threshold, and true damage is absorbed by shields like any other damage — so 'ignores your W shield' is flatly wrong. Also unstated anywhere: Feast's range is 175, meaning he has to be on top of you to cast it.
audit.why: A Nautilus who believes his shield does nothing against Feast plays the level-6 fight completely differently — and wrongly. The real rules are: armour and MR do not reduce it, Titan's Wrath still absorbs it, and he must close to 175 to use it at all.
audit.corrected: All seven fields restated as high true damage at 175 range on an 80s rank-1 cooldown that resistances do not cut. The percent-health and execute claims are gone, and the 'ignores your shield' claim is gone with them.
sources: enemyKit R text and cd 80/70/60 and range 175
enemyKit R percentHealth flag contradicted by description

audit.whatIsWrong: Chart rows 0, 1, 3 and 4 disagreed with the mirror audit's chart, and rows 3 and 4 disagreed with their own whys ('His scaling outpaces your flat power' and 'the all-in favors him' both sat under 'Skill').
audit.why: The mirror (chogath__nautilus) already fixed this chart to Nautilus / Nautilus / Cho'Gath / Cho'Gath / Cho'Gath / Cho'Gath / Cho'Gath and recorded that it deviates from the packet at level 2 deliberately, because the prose is unambiguous that the hook-plus-root all-in still wins there. Restating the same chart from this side keeps the two pages consistent; whys[1] was the one piece of prose that had to move with it.
audit.corrected: Chart set to match the mirror exactly in BOTH layers as matched pairs, ratings raised on the two Nautilus rows, and whys[1] rewritten to say why level 2 is Nautilus's rather than Cho'Gath's.

audit.whatIsWrong: Rupture was the tracked cooldown and the page said only 'Telegraphed. Dodge it.' — no number. Feral Scream's silence, the thing that actually breaks a Nautilus engage, was never given a cooldown or a range either.
audit.why: Rupture is on a flat 6 seconds. That changes the advice completely: you cannot trade around its downtime, you have to dodge the ground crack. Feral Scream is 11s at rank 1 in a 300-range cone, which is the real cooldown to bait before hooking.
audit.corrected: 6s and 11s/300 range written into breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, report[5].t, dontsFull[0].d and dontsFull[1].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: Itemisation recommended Plated Steelcaps with no reference to his damage types.
audit.why: Rupture, Feral Scream and Vorpal Spikes are all magic damage and Feast is true — armour is the one stat that does nothing in this matchup, which is exactly what the missingInteractions 'resistances-invalidated' rule is pointing at.
audit.corrected: report[8].t switched to Mercury's Treads and states the damage types.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 your trades stay decent but the lane is already tilting his way — every minute he survives is a Feast stack, and Feast stacks are HP you have to chew through with low base damage you don't have. At 6 your Depth Charge is a clean pick tool, but his R answers it: it's a true-damage percent execute that doesn't care about your bonus health or W shield. Don't solo all-in him at 6 hoping to burst — bring your jungler, use your R to start the gank, and convert your early lead into a tower or a kill before his stacks make him unkillable.

edits.before: This is his game and you have to accept it. A stacked Cho out-tanks you flat, and his true-damage R execute ignores every point of armor, health, and sustain you bought — you are the squishier tank in this fight by late game. Your job is no longer to win the 1v1; it's to be the CC-bot. Land Q-pull and R lockdown on his carries, peel for your own, and never facecheck him alone, because his R will execute you out of a 50%-HP screen and your anchor can't pull a kill out of that.
edits.after: This is his game and you have to accept it. A stacked Cho out-tanks you flat, and Feast's true damage ignores every point of armour and magic resist you bought — you are the squishier tank in this fight by late game. Your job is no longer to win the 1v1; it's to be the CC-bot. Land Q-pull and R lockdown on his carries, peel for your own, and never facecheck him alone at 175 range, because Feast takes a huge bite out of a full bar and your anchor can't pull a kill out of that.

notes: The dominant error was Feast being written as a 'true-damage percent execute' that 'ignores your shield' in seven places. Riot's text supports neither the percent nor the execute, and true damage is still absorbed by Titan's Wrath — a Nautilus who believes otherwise plays level 6 wrong. Feast's 175 range was also never mentioned, and it is the reason his ult is a melee-commit rather than a ranged threat. The 'grounding' flag on Rupture is not supported by Riot's description (knockup, damage and slow only) and no grounding claim was made — it would be doubly irrelevant since Nautilus has no dash. Following the mirror on the level chart, including its deliberate level-2 deviation from the packet chart, so the two pages agree. Sample is 16 games at exactly 50%.
